Name: Rigol DG1062Z Dual-Channel Function/Arbitrary Waveform Generator (DG1000Z Series, USB-TMC/LAN)
Notes: Built from docs/devices/rigol-dg1062z/programming-manual.md (RIGOL Programming Guide - DG1000Z Series, Feb. 2014, PGB09103-1110). The guide uses the DG1062Z as its worked example throughout and also covers the sibling DG1032Z (same command set; only the frequency-range table in :SOURce:FREQuency differs per-model). Remote interfaces are rear-panel USB-TMC (USB Device port) and LAN/LXI; GPIB is only reachable via an external GPIB-USB converter and is out of scope here, as is the optional :PA external power-amplifier accessory subsystem. This unit has the 16M point 'Arb 16M' memory option installed. Almost every SOURce/OUTPut/TRIGger command in this series takes an optional [<n>] channel selector immediately after the root keyword (e.g. SOURce2:FREQuency) rather than the older :CH2-suffix style DG1022 uses - modeled here as a Channel choice parameter substituted directly into the command keyword. Omitting/defaulting the selector always addresses CH1 regardless of whichever channel is selected on the front panel. Query replies are always returned in scientific notation with 7 significant digits, regardless of the unit suffix used on the corresponding set command. Enabling AM/FM/PM/FSK/ASK/PSK/PWM modulation, Sweep, or Burst on a channel automatically disables whichever of the other two modes was already active on that channel; Harmonic mode blocks all three and must be turned off first. Every :COUPling:* family (FREQuency/PHASe/AMPLitude) requires its MODE and DEViation/RATio to be set before its STATe is turned ON - changing MODE or DEViation/RATio while already ON is rejected. LAN configuration changes need BOTH SYSTem:COMMunicate:LAN:APPLy (applies live) and SYSTem:COMMunicate:LAN:UPDate (persists to nonvolatile memory) - APPLy alone reverts on power-cycle. Arbitrary-waveform point counts auto-adjust: 8-8192 points auto-interpolates to 8192 in frequency mode; >8192-16384 points auto-switches the channel to sample-rate mode - always verify the actual stored point count with TRACe:DATA:POINts? after a download rather than assuming the requested count was kept. OUTPut<n>:LOAD only corrects the instrument's own amplitude/offset computation for an assumed external load - it never changes the fixed 50-ohm physical source impedance. *OPC? blocks until all pending operations complete (a genuine sync point); *OPC merely sets a status-register bit asynchronously and returns immediately - prefer *OPC? after a DATA download or state recall before reading results back.
